source.title: Calendar feature geometry in GPT-2 layer 8 residual stream SAEs

record.tranche_reason: Measures the geometry and cross-size variation of SAE decoder features in GPT-2, bearing on indirect LLM evidence for SAE features and whether SAE features are stable canonical units; it does not use the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: The post reports measurements of SAE feature activations and decoder-direction geometry. Feature-selection criteria and the reported PCA/UMAP/clustering outcomes are included where the text states an outcome. Values or details visible only in figure captions without a textual outcome are not inferred.
record.test_reason: Compares SAE feature inventories for calendar concepts across GPT-2 SAE sizes (768 to 98304). This shows feature splitting, which bears on whether SAE features are stable, canonical units (V5). It also shows that SAEs recover interpretable sparse features (V4). The geometry, PCA and clustering results do not measure any version directly.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that GPT-2 SAE decoder directions are highly structured. They find a historical-time direction that orders non-date features by era and is not a principal component of the decoder matrix. They also note feature splitting across SAE sizes and offer clustering as a preliminary unsupervised way to find such structures, one that failed for weekdays and months and found mostly uninterpretable clusters.
record.recipe_differences: Uses GPT-2 layer 8 SAE decoder directions with PCA, UMAP, and HDBSCAN to study calendar-feature geometry; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature patterns vary with SAE size; single-year features are more evident in the largest SAEs. The clustering approach found year features but did not recover weekday or month clusters.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE decoder directions for year features are structured. A historical-time direction orders non-year features by era, and this direction is neither an SAE feature nor a global principal component.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE decoder space has interpretable low-dimensional structure across features, which individual features do not capture.

fits_no_version.finding: UMAP plus HDBSCAN on decoder directions recovers the year-feature cluster but not weekday or month clusters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unsupervised clustering can find some structured feature groups in SAE decoder space.

record.problems: The post describes the labeled non-year examples as manually selected, the historical ordering as imperfect, and the clustering approach as preliminary. It says the principal components of most features were not interpretable and acknowledges that this may reflect either the features or the clustering method.
record.rows_left_out: No separate row for the month-feature PCA plot: the post provides its caption but no distinct textual outcome beyond the general cross-size feature-splitting description in r3. Figure-only details without stated outcomes were not inferred.

untested.parts: No toy models, no sparsity transition, no capacity geometry.
Neuron polysemanticity and its capacity explanation are not examined.
Causes of polysemanticity are not examined.
Spread of features across neurons is not measured, and there is no quantitative reconstruction or interpretability rate.
Completeness, stability across seeds or models, and comparison with other extraction methods are not tested.
There is no test of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features. The circular weekday finding is cited from prior work (arXiv:2405.14860), not tested here.

missing.what: Month features also show the smallest SAE's single feature splitting into many specific features in larger SAEs.
Single-day weekday features from different SAE sizes form clusters in PCA space. This is partial cross-size consistency.
missing.locator: Features at different scales, after Figure 1

record.verdict_notes: This is a short Alignment Forum post. It has no controls and no uncertainty estimates, and the labelled examples are manually selected. Its main contribution is decoder geometry, which no version captures. The V5 challenge rests only on calendar features in one model and layer.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-versus-dimension capacity comparison, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular superposition geometry are tested.
Does not test neuron polysemanticity or whether feature importance and limited capacity determine dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not test causes of polysemantic neurons independent of capacity pressure.
Studies SAE features in GPT-2, but does not establish that the SAE recovers all underlying model features or measure their distribution across neurons.
Tests feature consistency across SAE sizes and some aspects of interpretability; does not establish completeness or stability across models, training runs, or other extraction methods.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features as explanations of superposition.

rows.subject: GPT-2 layer 8 residual stream SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Examined weekday feature activations and decoder-direction geometry.
rows.measure: Number and pattern of weekday features
rows.value: One weekday feature activated strongly on all days of the week.
rows.note: A single broadly activating feature is reported for the smallest SAE.
rows.check: Shows that an SAE recovers a sparse, interpretable weekday feature. On its own it says nothing about V5 stability; that comes from the comparison in r3.

rows.subject: GPT-2 layer 8 residual stream SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Examined weekday feature activations and decoder-direction geometry.
rows.measure: Number and pattern of weekday features
rows.value: 10 weekday features: 3 activated on all days of the week and 7 activated on a single day each.
rows.note: The post reports more specific weekday features in the largest SAE than in the 768-feature SAE.
rows.check: Interpretable weekday features are recovered. The V5 bearing belongs to the cross-size comparison in r3, not to this single-SAE count.

rows.subject: GPT-2 layer 8 residual stream SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Compared calendar-feature groupings across SAE sizes.
rows.value: The smallest SAE has a single feature that splits into many more specific features in larger SAEs; the post describes those specific features as seeming roughly equally important.
rows.note: The reported cross-size splitting bears against a stable, canonical feature inventory.
rows.check: For V5 the state should be absent, not reversed. A single feature splitting into many across sizes means there is no stable, canonical inventory. V4 is observed, since interpretable sparse features are recovered at every size.

source_check.correct: Use version-specific states: observed for V4; absent for V5. The 768-feature SAE has one weekday feature; the largest has ten, comprising three all-weekday features and seven single-day features.
source_check.locator_found: Features at different scales, paragraphs surrounding Figures 1–2; text lines 13–19.
source_check.problem: The shared absent state contradicts the recovery of interpretable calendar features under V4.

rows.subject: GPT-2 layer 8 residual stream SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Applied PCA to decoder directions of single-year features.
rows.measure: Whether the first two principal components organize the single-year features
rows.value: The method succeeds for only a few 21st-century features and for no 20th-century features.
rows.note: The post also notes a group of single-year features in a smaller SAE near the center of the plot, suggesting those principal components do not explain their variance.
rows.check: Whether PCA organizes single-year decoder directions is a geometry result. It does not measure any version.

rows.subject: GPT-2 layer 8 residual stream SAEs
rows.size_stated: largest SAEs; exact size not stated for this finding
rows.operation_detail: Examined calendar-year feature activation periods across SAE sizes.

conditions.value: across sizes; largest SAEs contrasted with smaller SAEs

rows.value: Only the largest SAEs have more than a few single-calendar-year features; most features activate on ranges of years or other patterns, such as the start and end of decades.
rows.locator: Features at different scales; Figure 4 description
rows.note: The text describes a mix of single-year, multi-year-range, and other period features.
rows.check: How specific the year features are depends on SAE size: single-year features appear mainly in the largest SAEs. This bears on stability across dictionary size. V4 is not separately informative here.

source_check.locator_found: Features at different scales, paragraph immediately before Figure 4; text line 21.

rows.subject: GPT-2 layer 8 residual stream SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Applied PCA to calendar-year features, including multi-year features.
rows.value: The calendar-year features are described as clearly arranged in a counter-clockwise direction.
rows.locator: Features at different scales; Figure 5 description
rows.note: The post says the more structured plot results from including multi-year features.
rows.check: The counter-clockwise PCA arrangement is decoder geometry and does not bear on any version.

rows.subject: GPT-2 layer 8 residual stream SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Projected non-year features onto polar-transformed principal components of calendar-year features.

conditions.value: randomly selected features for which a human could identify a clear time-period association

rows.measure: Ordering of non-year features by associated historical period
rows.value: The angle appears to align with increasing calendar year; the post gives Saddam Hussein before Barack Obama and Mitt Romney, followed by Donald Trump, as an example. The ordering is described as imperfect.
rows.note: The plotted x-axis hides 99.5% of the 49152-feature SAE, and the labeled examples were manually selected from a random subsample.
rows.check: The historical-time ordering of projected features is decoder-geometry structure, not a version's measure. The labelled points were also manually selected.

rows.subject: GPT-2 layer 8 residual stream SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Compared the historical-time direction with SAE features and PCA of the full decoder weight matrix.
rows.measure: Correspondence of the direction to an SAE feature or a principal component of the full decoder matrix
rows.value: The direction does not correspond to either an SAE feature or a PCA of the entire decoder weight matrix.
rows.note: This is evidence that the reported direction is not itself a canonical SAE feature or a principal component of the full decoder matrix.
rows.check: An interpretable direction that is not a single SAE feature or a global principal component does not show SAE incompleteness. It may be a combination of features. Move to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: GPT-2 layer 8 residual stream SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Applied UMAP to decoder directions, then HDBSCAN to the two-dimensional UMAP representation.
rows.measure: Whether clustering identifies a group corresponding to individual-year features
rows.value: HDBSCAN finds a cluster corresponding to the individual-year features.
rows.note: The post reports that the principal components from the automatically found cluster are very similar to those from the ground-truth year features.
rows.check: This is the authors' own unsupervised clustering method succeeding. It is method performance, not a result on the claim.

rows.subject: GPT-2 layer 8 residual stream SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Examined interpretability and recovery of clusters found from decoder directions.

conditions.value: clusters other than the reported year-feature cluster

rows.measure: Interpretability of cluster principal components and recovery of weekday/month clusters
rows.value: The principal components of the vast majority of features were not interpretable; the approach did not recover clusters corresponding to weekdays or months.
rows.note: The post says the lack of interpretability may reflect either features without interpretable linear relationships or a poor clustering approach.
rows.check: This is the authors' clustering method failing, and they attribute the failure possibly to the method itself. It is not evidence about the features.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small layer 8 residual SAEs, calendar features
relationships.reason: SAEs of all sizes recover sparse, interpretable weekday, month and year features (r1, r2, r3).
relationships.display_finding: SAEs of every size recovered sparse, interpretable weekday, month and year features.
